description: The playable scene US-3 of tasklist 146 ships: a guard, a dark courtyard and a wall the player can only climb once a skill says so. Two adopted mechanics end to end — PERCEPTION decides whether the guard notices, TRAVERSAL decides whether the wall can be climbed — and every decision is made by core's own rule packs inside libinsimul. Nothing in the engine reimplements one. AInsimulMechanicSampleScene reads this file, so changing the scenario changes the scene; ctest `activation_witness` reads the SAME file and executes it through insimul::InsimulKB, which is what makes 'the scene exercises them' a checked statement rather than a screenshot.

steps.name: the guard does not notice the player in the dark

hostFacts.note: FInsimulPerceptionProbe: the distance between the two AActor locations, converted from Unreal units into the sense's own range units
FInsimulPerceptionProbe: LineTraceSingleByChannel from the guard's eye socket to the target, obstructed by the crates

steps.then: the scene leaves the guard on patrol

steps.name: the wall refuses a player with no climbing skill

hostFacts.note: FInsimulTraversalProbe: the movement mode UCharacterMovementComponent reports when the pawn reaches the wall

steps.then: the scene plays the refusal and the player stays in the courtyard

steps.name: the same wall opens once the world grants the skill
steps.then: ILocomotionHost carries the body up; core decided that it MAY happen and never how it looks

steps.name: the lit torch is what the guard notices — the same query, a different world
an inactive module is ABSENT, not merely unpopulated
steps.then: the rpg bundle does not select stamina, so its pack was never consulted and its vocabulary does not exist in this KB — core's module contract §7.3, from inside the running scene
